Cameron County Elections Department to review three races as part of first statewide audit

Wednesday, November 18 2026
Nov 18, 2026

November 18, 2026
in
 News - Local 
Source: KRGV 
By: Armando Gomez 
 Share: 
 Brownsville, TX (KRGV) — The Texas Secretary of State is conducting a statewide risk-limiting audit and Cameron County will have three races reviewed.
 The audits are meant to check whether statewide election results match what was reported. In Cameron County, the races being looked at are the U.S. Senate race, the chief justice of the Texas Supreme Court race and the county clerk race.
 The county’s election warehouse securely stores paper ballots from the November elections. Soon, boxes from those three races will be opened and recounted.
 The audit was announced by Texas Secretary of State Robert S. Howden on Nov. 16.
 "Texans deserve to know their elections are secure and their votes are counted accurately," Howden said. "We have multiple checks and balances throughout the process and now we have two ways to verify the results after the election." 
 According to a news release from the office of the Texas Secretary of State, the Nov. 3 general election marks the first implementation of statewide risk-limiting audits required under Texas law. These audits use statistical methods and randomly selected paper ballots to verify reported outcomes in selected statewide contests. The process provides an independent check of electronic tabulation results against paper ballots. 
 Similar audits are conducted in 16 other states.
 Brownsville resident Diana Coronado, who voted in Cameron County on Election Day, said she does not think there should be a reason for a recount.
 "In my opinion, I don't think there should be a reason to do a recount giving that when you go to vote they already check there. They check your ID," Coronado said.
 She said she thinks a recount makes sense only if a race is statistically close.
 "If it is statistically close, and someone wants to contest the results, well yeah. If a certain amendment or whatever passed by significant amount I don't see a need for recount," Coronado said.
 Cameron County Elections Administrator Remi Garza said the audit looks for the statistical probability that the reported outcome can be repeated through a random selection of ballots across Texas.
 "It is looking for the statistic probability that the outcome of the election reported can be repeated by doing this random selection of ballots throughout the state of Texas by one race or more," Garza said.
 Garza said the state chose two of the races and Cameron County chose the third.
 "We know we are going to have an initial round, and they may call for a second round but ultimately if they are unable to reconcile it or it doesn't fall within the statistical limits, the secretary of state may call for a hand count of that particular race," Garza said.
 Coronado said she hopes the recount is being done for the right reasons.
 "To do a recount just because somebody cries foul, I don't think it is right. If it's close and there is a statistical error, then yeah," Coronado said.
 The audit will happen at the Cameron County Courthouse's Dancy Building. It will begin on Thursday, Nov. 19, at 9 a.m. and is not open to the public, but candidates can send poll watchers.
